title: Interactive Digital Media PanPinRu as an Effort to Increase Interest in Learning Students in Linear Equations of One Variable
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an interactive digital mathematics medium, PanPinRu (Segment Moving Board), can improve junior high school students’ interest and achievement in learning one-variable linear equations. The motivation is the persistent problem of low student engagement and weak understanding of abstract algebra topics in conventional, teacher-centered mathematics instruction.

The intervention is a web-based, gamified digital application that lets students manipulate variables and constants virtually, receive automatic feedback, and complete game-like challenges. The study uses a Design-Based Research approach with iterative cycles of needs analysis, design/development, classroom implementation, revision, and evaluation, involving collaboration among researchers, a mathematics teacher, and students.

The population studied was class VII A students at SMP Darul Ulum 5 Grati in Indonesia, with teachers participating in development and implementation. Data came from observations, questionnaires on learning interest, interviews, and pretest/posttest learning outcome measures, analyzed using both quantitative and qualitative methods. The paper reports that PanPinRu increased students’ learning interest and produced learning outcomes above the achievement criterion, suggesting that interactive digital and gamified media can be an effective way to support mathematics learning in this topic and setting.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a design-based research/mixed-methods classroom study in a single class, with descriptive quantitative analysis and qualitative feedback. It is peer-reviewed, but there is no clear comparison group or randomized design, so causal evidence is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported outcomes are positive for a priority population, but the magnitude is unclear because no effect size, confidence interval, or comparison condition is provided. The evidence suggests promising impact, but it is modest/uncertain rather than clearly large.

interventions.use_case: interactive digital PanPinRu segment-moving board for one-variable linear equations, with virtual manipulation of variables/constants, automatic feedback, and gamified challenges

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports improved mathematics learning outcomes after use of the interactive digital PanPinRu media for one-variable linear equations. The average learning outcome score was 84.74, exceeding the Learning Objective Achievement Criteria (KKTP); the study describes this as a significant improvement, but does not report a formal effect size or inferential statistic in the excerpt.
finding.measure: math learning outcome test (pretest/posttest; average post-implementation score)

finding.finding_summary: Student learning interest increased after the intervention, with an average student response score of 65.57 categorized as an increased category. The study concludes that the interactive digital/gamified design significantly raised motivation and engagement, though no inferential statistics or effect size are reported.
finding.measure: learning interest questionnaire / student response score
